topic.readerProblem: A store owner or marketer wants ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI to name and correctly describe their products, and needs to know what to change on an individual product page and how to check whether it worked.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether AI engines recommend a brand when buyers ask. The page covers the product-page layer of that problem (readable facts, matching markup and feeds, crawl access) and points to AEOeye's crawler access study and free audit as ways to check.

assessment: The page now answers how to optimize a single product page for AI answers in the first screen, then walks through how engines read a page (server HTML, no JavaScript execution by most AI crawlers as of the December 2024 Vercel/MERJ data), the answer block, spec/price/availability exposure and variant URLs, Product markup and the product feed route, comparison and FAQ content, and a four-layer verification routine. It rests on Google Search Central and Merchant Center documentation, OpenAI's product feed spec and crawler documentation, Perplexity's crawler documentation, a University of Toronto paper, a SparkToro run-to-run study and AEOeye's own crawler access study (e-commerce and consumer group, with its convenience-sample caveats). It deliberately does not claim that ChatGPT or Perplexity read JSON-LD, that schema wins recommendations, or that FAQ markup still earns a Google rich result; it drops the earlier page's unsourced claims (engines cross-check markup, reviews quoted verbatim in AI answers, several engines ignore JSON-LD) and its incorrect description of the free audit.

sources.supports: Merchant Center landing page requirements: price, currency and availability must match product data; do not change displayed product information after initial loading because crawlers treat the post-load page as final; pre-select the variant in the landing page URL; include product structured data in the initial HTML.

Googlebot compares the price in the data source with the landing page or structured data price and may disapprove a mismatched product; it reads the HTML returned by the server, so prices added dynamically after load trigger an error.
Merchant listing requirements: name, image and an Offer with price and priceCurrency are required; aggregateRating, brand.name, gtin, availability and hasMerchantReturnPolicy are recommended.
General structured data policies: do not mark up content that is not visible to readers; when marking up reviews, include all of the reviews that are visible on the page.

Google's guide to generative AI features: first-hand perspective vs a summary of existing content; structured data isn't required for generative AI search and there is no special schema.org markup; Merchant Center feeds and Business Profiles can help products appear in AI responses.
Google Search Central changelog: the FAQ rich result feature no longer appears in Google Search starting May 7, 2026.

OpenAI product feed spec: nine required fields (item_id, title, description, url, brand, seller_name, image_url, availability, price); one row per variant with its own URL, price, availability; omitted or unrecognized availability rejects the row; plain-text factual descriptions.

OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search; sites opted out of OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers. The page describes the purpose of each bot and does not describe JSON-LD handling.

PerplexityBot surfaces and links sites in Perplexity search results; the page recommends allowing it in robots.txt and, for WAF users, allowing its user agent and published IP ranges. It does not describe JSON-LD handling.
Vercel and MERJ, published 2024-12-17: none of the major AI crawlers measured (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, ByteDance, Perplexity) rendered JavaScript; Gemini uses Googlebot's rendering infrastructure.

University of Toronto GEO paper: in US consumer-electronics queries AI search (a gpt-4o-search-preview model) cited earned media (independent reviews and comparison sites) for 92.1% of sources, read in the paper's results text.

SparkToro: 600 volunteers, 2,961 runs on ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI; under a 1 in 100 chance that ChatGPT or Google AI give the same list of brands in two responses; 60-100 runs per prompt suggested.
Definition of JSON-LD as a file format for encoding linked data using JSON.
